summary: Only two videos so far, so treat this as an early signal, not proof. The Hindi PIR sensor video did far better: about 1,850 total views, with shares and saves on Instagram, because it opened by busting a myth ('it doesn't actually see you'). The English Arduino video got only 157 views on YouTube and was never posted to Instagram, so it had less reach and a weaker, generic hook.
winningPattern: One everyday sensor or device people already interact with (motion lights, doors, phones), explained in Hindi. The hook is a myth-bust or surprising contradiction ('X aapko dekhta nahi!'). The title follows the pattern Hindi shock statement + 'Kaise Kaam Karta Hai?' + 🤔. Post to both Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts; Instagram currently brings about 3x the views and all the shares and saves.
doMore: Open every video with a myth or 'you think X, but actually Y' line in the first 2 seconds
Narrate in Hindi and use the 'Kaise Kaam Karta Hai?' title format consistently
Cross-post every video to Instagram Reels and YouTube Shorts on the same day
Pick sensors people meet in daily life (lights, doors, phones, ATMs) rather than dev boards
End with a save/share prompt like 'Save karo, project mein kaam aayega'
stopDoing: Posting to YouTube only and skipping Instagram
Generic 'How X actually works' hooks with no surprise or myth
Switching to English until Hindi results are tested at larger volume

bestTimes.reason: Indian Shorts/Reels prime time (lunch 12:30 and evening 19:30 IST) until we have enough of our own data
